t: This is where Sass's Academy once stood, a drawing school that no longer exists. Henry Sass, an English artist and teacher, founded it to prepare students for entry to the Royal Academy. It became an important art school, and many distinguished British painters received their early training here. Sass was so committed to teaching that Sir David Wilkie said he could have taught a stone to draw. So picture a room full of young artists, learning the basics before moving on to the great institution.
